title: Maximal chains of primes in a polynomial ring over a field have length the difference of the heights
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$ an integer and $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset P$ let $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\in\{0,1,2,\dots,\infty\}$ be the supremum of the integers $t\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\mathfrak q_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_t$ of prime ideals of $P$ with $\mathfrak q_t\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Then $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\le n$ for every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $P$, and for prime ideals $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ of $P$ every maximal chain of primes between $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak q$, that is, every chain $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_t=\mathfrak q$ of prime ideals of $P$ such that for each $1\le i\le t$ no prime ideal $\mathfrak r$ of $P$ satisfies $\mathfrak p_{i-1}\subsetneq\mathfrak r\subsetneq\mathfrak p_i$, has length $t=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)$.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak r\subset P$ be any prime ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring] (Proposition 00OQ) $P$ is a regular ring: $P$ is Noetherian and $P_{\mathfrak r}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], i.e. a Noetherian local ring, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak rP_{\mathfrak r}$, whose Krull dimension $d_{\mathfrak r}=\dim P_{\mathfrak r}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] is a non-negative integer and whose maximal ideal is generated by $d_{\mathfrak r}$ elements $y_1,\dots,y_{d_{\mathfrak r}}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OR (lemma-dimension-height-polynomial-ring, line 27737), proof, first sentence: 'By Proposition 00OQ any local ring of k[x_1,...,x_n] is regular'

proof.text: Choose a finite generating set of the maximal ideal of each regular local ring $P_{\mathfrak r}$ from step 1 of cardinality its spanFinrank, using Mathlib Submodule.FG.exists_span_finset_card_eq_spanFinrank. Its list is a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] this list is a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Unfolding [def-weil-pbc-depth], its length is a member of the supremum defining depth (or depth is infinity). Thus depth is at least the dimension, including dimension zero. This supplies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-maximal-chain-length].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OR (lemma-dimension-height-polynomial-ring, line 27737), proof, second sentence: 'Hence all local rings are Cohen-Macaulay, see Lemma 00NQ' (lemma-regular-ring-CM, line 25732)

proof.text: Heights. For a prime $\mathfrak r$ of $P$ the height $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak r)$ of the statement is, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], equal to $\dim P_{\mathfrak r}=d_{\mathfrak r}$; in particular it is a finite integer by step 1. If $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak r'$ are primes, every chain of primes ending inside $\mathfrak r$ ends inside $\mathfrak r'$, so $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak r)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak r')$. Given a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $P$, it is a proper ideal, so by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] there is a maximal ideal $\mathfrak M\supseteq\mathfrak q$, and $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak M)=\dim P_{\mathfrak M}=n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-maximal-localization-dimension] (Lemma 00OP). This is the first assertion.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OR (lemma-dimension-height-polynomial-ring, line 27737), proof, third sentence: 'The local rings at maximal ideals have dimension n' (Lemma 00OP, lemma-dim-affine-space, line 27660); the bound ht(q) <= n is the statement's first clause, written out here

proof.text: For the lower prime p, use Mathlib Ideal.exists_ltSeries_length_eq_height to choose an LTSeries a ending at p of length ht(p). In a maximally long series Mathlib Order.height_eq_index_of_length_eq_height_last identifies the height of every element with its index. Consequently its head has height zero and is minimal (Order.height_eq_zero). Each consecutive pair is a cover: a prime strictly between them would increase height at least once on each side by Order.height_add_one_le, forcing i+2 <= i+1. This constructs the saturated prefix without needing that P is a domain or identifying its head explicitly with (0). The private Lean helper saturated_of_full_height proves these order facts; no unproved helper is introduced.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OR (lemma-dimension-height-polynomial-ring, line 27737), proof, fourth sentence: 'Hence every maximal chain of primes between (0) and p has length height(p)' (only the existence of one such chain of length height(p) is needed, and it is written out here from the definition of the height instead of through Lemma 00NA)

proof.text: Concatenate the prefix a from step 4 with the given chain c using RelSeries.smash; the endpoint equalities identify a.last with c.head. The length is a.length+c.length. The private helper smash_saturated proves saturation by splitting the indices with Fin.addCases and applying the cover hypotheses on the two pieces. All primes in the concatenated chain are below its last prime q. By [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization], in the PrimeSpectrum form IsLocalization.AtPrime.primeSpectrumOrderIso, map this chain from the interval of primes below q to PrimeSpectrum of P_q [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The mapped chain still has a minimal head, maximal last element, and covers between consecutive elements. The private helper saturated_isMaxChain shows that it is a maximal chain: any point comparable with its entire range is below the last point; take the least index j whose value is above the point. At j=0 minimality forces equality. Otherwise comparability and minimality of j put the point strictly above the predecessor, and the cover condition forces equality with the jth element. Therefore no larger chain exists. This is precisely the maximal-chain hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-maximal-chain-length].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OR (lemma-dimension-height-polynomial-ring, line 27737), proof, last sentence: 'Putting these together leads to the assertion of the lemma' (written out); primes of a localization: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00E3

proof.text: Conclusion. $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is a Noetherian local ring of finite dimension $d=\dim P_{\mathfrak q}=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$ (steps 1 and 3) which is Cohen–Macaulay (step 2). By [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-maximal-chain-length] (Lemma 00N9) applied to $S=P_{\mathfrak q}$ and the maximal chain of step 5, its length equals $d$: $h+t=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$. Since $h=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)$, $t=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)$.

split_report.summary: Six steps following Stacks 00OR: P is a regular ring (00OQ, Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring), so every P_r is regular local; regular local rings are CM (00NQ node: a generating set of dim many elements is a regular sequence, depth >= dim); ht(r) = dim P_r finite, monotone, and ht(q) <= ht(M) = n by the 00OP node (first clause of the statement, which 00OR itself does not state); a chain realizing ht(p) is saturated and starts at (0) since P is a domain; concatenated with the given maximal chain it becomes, through the prime correspondence of the localization (00E3 leaf), a maximal chain of P_q; 00N9 (accepted node) gives its length = dim P_q = ht(q). The source's appeal to 00NA ('see Lemma 00NA for example') is replaced by this direct use of 00N9 in P_q (00NA's proof is 'follows immediately from 00N9'), so no 00NA node is created. No new nodes. Tags verified in tags/tags: 00OR, 00OQ, 00NQ, 00N9, 00NA, 00OP (the brief's guesses 00NJ/00NM are wrong). No citer of the item (00OS) or of its citers is used.

lean.statement: theorem maximalChain_height_difference {k : Type u} [Field k] (n : ℕ) (q : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) [q.IsPrime] : q.height ≤ (n : ℕ∞) ∧ ∀ (p : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) [p.IsPrime], p ≤ q → ∀ (c : LTSeries (PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k))), c.head.asIdeal = p → c.last.asIdeal = q → (∀ i : Fin c.length, c i.castSucc ⋖ c i.succ) → (c.length : ℕ∞) = q.height - p.height

reviewed_lean.note: k field {k:Type u}; n:ℕ incl. 0; P = MvPolynomial (Fin n) k; q prime [q.IsPrime]; ht = Ideal.height (prime case = sup of strict chains below q); ht(q) ≤ n first conjunct; p prime, p ≤ q; chain as LTSeries (PrimeSpectrum P) head p last q; saturation as CovBy (Iff.rfl to no prime strictly between); t = c.length; (t:ℕ∞) = q.height - p.height truncated sub safe as both ≤ n; t=0/p=q covered
